GSE260661: circulating miRNAs during FOLFOX chemotherapy

Plasma miRNAs of colorectal cancer patients during FOLFOX: ≥6 vs ≤3 cycles (paired)

2026-11-21

8 × 2
patients × draws

miRNAs tested

miRNAs at FDR < 0.05 (paired)

Study design

Plasma of 8 colorectal cancer patients on FOLFOX (5-fluorouracil, leucovorin, oxaliplatin) at Pusan National University Hospital, each sampled twice: an early draw after 2–3 cycles and a late draw after 6–8 cycles. Small RNA-seq (NEBNext, NextSeq 550, 75 bp single-end); the authors deposited one raw count file per sample (2,588 mature miRNAs, miRBase). Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) was graded with NCI-CTCAE v4.03 at each draw.

There is no untreated control group: every patient received FOLFOX. The analysis therefore asks how circulating miRNAs change within the same patient as exposure accumulates, and whether that change follows the worsening of neuropathy. Time on treatment, cumulative oxaliplatin dose and CIPN grade all increase together, so the late-vs-early effect cannot be attributed to any one of them (nor separated from disease course or other drugs).

Source: Ju Y, Baek DH, Choi GE, Jang A. Exploring microRNA patterns as biomarkers of FOLFOX chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy in patients with colorectal cancer. BBA Mol Basis Dis 1870 (2024) 167209, doi:10.1016/j.bbadis.2024.167209.

  • early: first draw, 2–3 FOLFOX cycles (8 samples).
  • late: second draw, 6–8 FOLFOX cycles (8 samples).

GEO metadata

The sample characteristics in GEO do not match the paper for 5 of 16 samples (cycles differ in 5, grade in 3). GEO lists the late draws almost uniformly as "7 cycles & grade 2". This analysis uses the values of the paper's Table 1 (data/samples.tsv); the comparison is in results/geo_metadata_check.tsv.

What the authors did

The authors treated the early and late draws as independent groups (ExDEGA, unadjusted p < 0.05 and fold change > 2) and reported two miRNAs higher in the late draw, miR-222-3p and miR-3184-5p. In a separate qPCR cohort of 27 patients (12 with ≤3 and 15 with ≥6 cycles; no sequencing data) only miR-3184-5p differed (ROC AUC 0.78). They did not use the pairing and did not correct for the 2,588 tests.

Pipeline

  1. prepare (01_prepare_geo.R): reads the 16 GEO count files (raw reads per mature miRNA), joins the curated sample sheet and checks it against GEO.
  2. differential (02_differential_expression.R): filter (≥ 10 reads in ≥ 8 samples), TMM normalization, QC plots and one edgeR quasi-likelihood fit per model (glmQLFit(robust = TRUE), glmQLFTest).
  3. targets (03_targets.R): validated targets (multiMiR: mirtarbase, mirecords) of every tested miRNA; miRTarBase limited to strong evidence = True.
  4. kegg_annotation: KEGG hsa gene–pathway table, downloaded once.
  5. enrichment (04_target_enrichment.R): GO BP and KEGG over-representation of the targets of the DE miRNAs of the paired model, against the targets of all tested miRNAs.
  6. report: this page.

DE miRNAs: unadjusted p < 0.01 and |log2FC| > 0.5 in every model (no miRNA reaches FDR < 0.05 in the primary model). The lists are exploratory: FDR is reported in every table. Positive log2FC = higher in the late draw.

Input data and quality control

Libraries have 1.7–5.9 M reads mapped to miRBase, but only 207–389 of the 2,588 annotated miRNAs have at least one read per sample, and 92–238 have ≥ 10 reads. The ten most abundant miRNAs take 72–90% of each library (the most abundant one is let-7b-5p, let-7f-5p, miR-122-5p, miR-451a). After filtering, 119 miRNAs are tested.

# Share of each library taken by the 10 most abundant miRNAs (over all samples)
top10 <- names(sort(rowSums(cpm_all), decreasing = TRUE))[1:10]
share <- as.data.frame(t(dge_all$counts[top10, ]) / colSums(dge_all$counts)) |>
  rownames_to_column("sample_id") |>
  mutate(other = 1 - rowSums(across(all_of(top10))), label = sample_label[sample_id]) |>
  pivot_longer(c(all_of(top10), other), names_to = "mirna", values_to = "share") |>
  mutate(mirna = factor(sub("^hsa-", "", mirna), levels = c(sub("^hsa-", "", top10), "other")))
save_plot(out$top_mirnas,
          ggplot(share, aes(x = label, y = share, fill = mirna)) +
            geom_col() + coord_flip() +
            scale_fill_manual(values = c(scales::hue_pal()(10), "grey80")) +
            scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
            labs(x = NULL, y = "Share of reads", fill = "miRNA") + theme_bw(base_size = 11),
          width = 8, height = 5.5)

From 02_differential_expression.R

Hemolysis

Red blood cells release miR-451a into plasma; the ratio miR-451a / miR-23a-3p is a common hemolysis indicator (in qPCR, ΔCq > 7 ≈ a 128-fold ratio, log2 = 7). Sequencing ratios are not on the same scale, so use the plot to spot samples that stand out, and pairs where one draw differs from the other.

# Hemolysis ratio: log2((CPM miR-451a + 1) / (CPM miR-23a-3p + 1)), paired lines per patient
num <- cfg$qc$hemolysis_numerator
den <- cfg$qc$hemolysis_denominator
if (all(c(num, den) %in% rownames(cpm_all))) {
  hem <- tibble(sample_id = colnames(cpm_all), patient = coldata$patient, timepoint = coldata$timepoint,
                ratio = log2((cpm_all[num, ] + 1) / (cpm_all[den, ] + 1)),
                den_zero = dge_all$counts[den, ] == 0)
  save_plot(out$hemolysis,
            ggplot(hem, aes(x = timepoint, y = ratio, group = patient)) +
              geom_line(colour = "grey60") +
              geom_point(aes(colour = timepoint, shape = den_zero), size = 3) +
              geom_text_repel(data = hem[hem$timepoint == trt_level, ], aes(label = patient),
                              nudge_x = 0.15, size = 3, direction = "y") +
              scale_colour_manual(values = tp_colors) +
              scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 16, `TRUE` = 4),
                                 labels = c(`FALSE` = "detected", `TRUE` = "0 reads")) +
              labs(x = NULL, y = sprintf("log2 (%s + 1) / (%s + 1), CPM", sub("^hsa-", "", num),
                                         sub("^hsa-", "", den)),
                   colour = "Timepoint", shape = sub("^hsa-", "", den)) +
              theme_bw(base_size = 12),
            width = 6.5, height = 5)
} else {
  placeholder_plot(out$hemolysis, "Hemolysis miRNAs not in the count table")
}

# MDS of log2 CPM (limma plotMDS on the tested miRNAs), the two draws of a patient joined
mds <- plotMDS(logcpm, top = min(500, nrow(logcpm)), plot = FALSE)
mds_df <- tibble(sample_id = colnames(logcpm), x = mds$x, y = mds$y,
                 patient = coldata$patient, timepoint = coldata$timepoint)
save_plot(out$mds,
          ggplot(mds_df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
            geom_line(aes(group = patient), colour = "grey70") +
            geom_point(aes(colour = timepoint), size = 3.5) +
            geom_text_repel(aes(label = patient), size = 3) +
            scale_colour_manual(values = tp_colors) +
            labs(x = sprintf("Leading logFC dim 1 (%.0f%%)", 100 * mds$var.explained[1]),
                 y = sprintf("Leading logFC dim 2 (%.0f%%)", 100 * mds$var.explained[2]),
                 colour = "Timepoint") +
            theme_bw(base_size = 12),
          width = 7, height = 5.5)

From 02_differential_expression.R

# Pearson correlation of log2 CPM centred per miRNA (so the shared plasma profile does not dominate)
centred <- logcpm - rowMeans(logcpm)
cc <- cor(centred)
dimnames(cc) <- list(sample_label[rownames(cc)], sample_label[colnames(cc)])
ann <- data.frame(timepoint = coldata$timepoint, row.names = sample_label[coldata$sample_id])
save_plot(out$correlation,
          pheatmap(cc, annotation_row = ann, annotation_col = ann,
                   annotation_colors = list(timepoint = tp_colors),
                   color = colorRampPalette(c("#3B4CC0", "white", "#B40426"))(101),
                   breaks = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 102), display_numbers = TRUE, number_format = "%.1f",
                   fontsize_number = 6, silent = TRUE)$gtable,
          width = 9, height = 8)

From 02_differential_expression.R

Model: paired

~ patient + timepoint, coefficient timepointlate. Within-patient change from the early to the late draw (primary analysis).

No miRNAs reach FDR < 0.05 (smallest FDR: 0.135); the DE list uses the unadjusted p-value. 3 miRNAs have p < 0.01 where 1.2 are expected by chance; with the fold-change cutoff, 3 remain (3 up, 0 down). Treat them as exploratory.

# Volcano: log2FC vs -log10 p; DE miRNAs coloured, top 10 and the paper's candidates labelled
vd <- tt |> mutate(
  class = case_when(mirna %in% hits$mirna & log2FoldChange > 0 ~ "up",
                    mirna %in% hits$mirna & log2FoldChange < 0 ~ "down", TRUE ~ "ns"),
  lab = ifelse(mirna %in% c(head(tt$mirna, 10), candidates), sub("^hsa-", "", mirna), NA))
save_plot(out$volcano[[i]],
          ggplot(vd, aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(pvalue))) +
            geom_point(aes(colour = class), size = 1.8, alpha = 0.8) +
            geom_text_repel(aes(label = lab), size = 3, max.overlaps = 30, na.rm = TRUE) +
            geom_vline(xintercept = c(-lfc_cut, lfc_cut), linetype = 3, colour = "grey50") +
            geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(p_line), linetype = 3, colour = "grey50") +
            scale_colour_manual(values = c(up = "#CC0000", down = "#3399FF", ns = "grey70"),
                                breaks = c("up", "down")) +
            labs(x = "log2 fold change", y = "-log10 p-value", colour = NULL,
                 subtitle = sprintf("%s (%s): %d up, %d down at %s < %g and |log2FC| > %g", n,
                                    models[[n]]$formula, sum(vd$class == "up"), sum(vd$class == "down"),
                                    ifelse(rule$col == "padj", "FDR", "p"), rule$cut, lfc_cut)) +
            theme_bw(base_size = 12),
          width = 7.5, height = 5.5)

~ timepoint, coefficient timepointlate. Late vs early as independent groups, as in the paper (for reference).

Top miRNAs within patients

# Top miRNAs of the primary model (by p-value): log2 CPM centred within each patient
tt_p <- fits[[primary]]$table
top <- head(tt_p$mirna, cfg$plots$heatmap_max_mirnas %||% 40)
within <- logcpm[top, , drop = FALSE]
for (p in levels(coldata$patient)) {
  s <- coldata$sample_id[coldata$patient == p]
  within[, s] <- within[, s] - rowMeans(within[, s, drop = FALSE])
}
ord <- coldata$sample_id[order(coldata$timepoint, coldata$patient)]
within <- within[, ord]
colnames(within) <- sample_label[ord]
rownames(within) <- sub("^hsa-", "", rownames(within))
lim <- max(abs(within))
save_plot(out$heatmap,
          pheatmap(within, cluster_cols = FALSE, annotation_col = ann,
                   annotation_colors = list(timepoint = tp_colors),
                   color = colorRampPalette(c("#3399FF", "white", "#CC0000"))(101),
                   breaks = seq(-lim, lim, length.out = 102), fontsize_row = 7, silent = TRUE,
                   gaps_col = sum(coldata$timepoint == ref_level))$gtable,
          width = 8, height = 2 + 0.14 * length(top))

From 02_differential_expression.R

Paired vs unpaired

The paired model removes the between-patient differences from the residual variance. Where it gains power, miRNAs lie above the diagonal on the x-axis side; where the patient effect is weak, the two models agree.

# Primary model against each other model: -log10 p of the same miRNA
others <- setdiff(names(fits), primary)
cmp <- bind_rows(lapply(others, function(n) {
  inner_join(fits[[primary]]$table |> dplyr::select(mirna, p_primary = pvalue),
             fits[[n]]$table |> dplyr::select(mirna, p_other = pvalue), by = "mirna") |>
    mutate(model = n)
}))
if (nrow(cmp)) {
  save_plot(out$model_comparison,
            ggplot(cmp, aes(x = -log10(p_primary), y = -log10(p_other))) +
              geom_abline(linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
              geom_point(aes(colour = mirna %in% candidates), size = 1.6, alpha = 0.8) +
              geom_text_repel(data = cmp[cmp$mirna %in% candidates, ], aes(label = sub("^hsa-", "", mirna)),
                              size = 3) +
              scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey40", `TRUE` = "#CC0000"), guide = "none") +
              facet_wrap(~ model) +
              labs(x = sprintf("-log10 p, %s model", primary), y = "-log10 p, other model") +
              theme_bw(base_size = 12),
            width = 4 + 3.5 * length(others), height = 4.5)
} else {
  placeholder_plot(out$model_comparison, "Only one model")
}

From 02_differential_expression.R

The paper's candidate miRNAs

  • miR-3184-5p: 18,668 reads in total, detected in 16 of 16 libraries (≥ 10 reads in 12); higher in the late draw in 6 of 8 patients (median paired change +2.27 log2 CPM, paired Wilcoxon p = 0.107). edgeR: paired log2FC +3.37, p = 0.0773, FDR = 0.761; unpaired log2FC +3.08, p = 0.0209, FDR = 0.623; cipn_worsening log2FC -2.51, p = 0.463, FDR = 0.961.
  • miR-222-3p: 3,156 reads in total, detected in 13 of 16 libraries (≥ 10 reads in 9); higher in the late draw in 7 of 8 patients (median paired change +1.58 log2 CPM, paired Wilcoxon p = 0.0209). edgeR: paired log2FC +4.04, p = 0.0107, FDR = 0.32; unpaired log2FC +2.71, p = 0.0399, FDR = 0.792; cipn_worsening log2FC -1.11, p = 0.608, FDR = 0.961.
# Candidate miRNAs of the paper: log2(CPM + 1) per patient at both draws (every miRNA, before filtering)
cand_present <- intersect(candidates, rownames(cpm_all))
if (length(cand_present)) {
  cd <- as.data.frame(t(log2(cpm_all[cand_present, , drop = FALSE] + 1))) |>
    rownames_to_column("sample_id") |>
    pivot_longer(-sample_id, names_to = "mirna", values_to = "log2cpm") |>
    mutate(patient = coldata[sample_id, "patient"], timepoint = coldata[sample_id, "timepoint"],
           mirna = sub("^hsa-", "", mirna))
  save_plot(out$candidates_plot,
            ggplot(cd, aes(x = timepoint, y = log2cpm, group = patient)) +
              geom_line(colour = "grey60") +
              geom_point(aes(colour = timepoint), size = 3) +
              geom_text_repel(data = cd[cd$timepoint == trt_level, ], aes(label = patient),
                              nudge_x = 0.15, size = 3, direction = "y") +
              scale_colour_manual(values = tp_colors) +
              facet_wrap(~ mirna, scales = "free_y") +
              labs(x = NULL, y = "log2 (CPM + 1)", colour = "Timepoint") +
              theme_bw(base_size = 12),
            width = 4 + 3 * length(cand_present), height = 4.5)
} else {
  placeholder_plot(out$candidates_plot, "No candidate miRNA in the count table")
}

Validated targets and enrichment

119 of the 119 tested miRNAs have validated targets in multiMiR, covering 10,078 genes (the enrichment universe). The DE miRNAs of the paired model (3 exploratory, p < 0.01) have 463 validated targets (up: 463). Over-representation uses the targets of all tested miRNAs as background, so it asks what is special about the targets of the changed miRNAs among the targets of plasma miRNAs in general. Validated-target databases are biased towards well-studied miRNAs and genes, and a target list says nothing about whether the miRNA acts on it in the tissue that matters (here, peripheral nerve).

# Top GO BP and KEGG terms per direction (by adjusted p), gene ratio and adjusted p
top_terms <- bind_rows(
  if (nrow(go)) go |> mutate(source = "GO BP") else NULL,
  if (nrow(kegg)) kegg |> mutate(source = "KEGG") else NULL
)
if (nrow(top_terms)) {
  top_terms <- top_terms |>
    mutate(ratio = sapply(strsplit(GeneRatio, "/"), function(x) as.numeric(x[1]) / as.numeric(x[2]))) |>
    group_by(source, direction) |> slice_min(p.adjust, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |> ungroup() |>
    mutate(Description = stringr::str_trunc(Description, 60),
           label = reorder(paste(Description, direction, sep = "___"), -log10(p.adjust)))
  save_plot(out$dotplot,
            ggplot(top_terms, aes(x = ratio, y = label, size = Count, colour = -log10(p.adjust))) +
              geom_point() +
              scale_y_discrete(labels = function(x) sub("___.*$", "", x)) +
              scale_colour_gradient(low = "#3399FF", high = "#CC0000") +
              facet_grid(source ~ direction, scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
              labs(x = "Gene ratio", y = NULL, colour = "-log10 padj", size = "Genes") +
              theme_bw(base_size = 10),
            width = 11, height = 2 + 0.22 * nrow(top_terms))
} else {
  placeholder_plot(out$dotplot, "No DE miRNA with validated targets, or no enriched term")
}

From 04_target_enrichment.R

Interpretation and limitations

  • No control group. Every change is relative to the same patient's earlier draw. It reflects cumulative FOLFOX exposure, but also time, disease course, surgery recovery and supportive medication, and it cannot be attributed to oxaliplatin or to neuropathy specifically.
  • Small and sparse. 8 patients, 119 miRNAs with enough reads; the paired model finds 0 miRNAs at FDR < 0.05.
  • The paper's candidates: miR-3184-5p (paired p = 0.0773, FDR = 0.761); miR-222-3p (paired p = 0.0107, FDR = 0.32). The authors used unadjusted p < 0.05 and unpaired groups; with ~2,600 miRNAs some hits are expected by chance.
  • CIPN. The cipn_worsening model asks whether the change is larger in patients whose grade rose more; with Δgrade of 0, +1 or +2 in only 8 patients, it can only flag large effects.

Configuration

Show config.yaml
# ============================================================
# Dataset configuration (GSE260661). The scripts in ../scripts/mirna/ are dataset-agnostic: everything
# that differs between datasets is here.
# ============================================================

dataset: GSE260661
title: "Plasma miRNAs of colorectal cancer patients during FOLFOX: ≥6 vs ≤3 cycles (paired)"

# GEO per-sample count files (one tab-separated file per GSM: miRNA name + raw read count). The tar is
# downloaded and extracted into data/ only when raw_dir is missing; series_soft is used to compare the GEO
# characteristics with the curated sample sheet.
input:
  geo_accession: GSE260661
  raw_tar_url: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE260nnn/GSE260661/suppl/GSE260661_RAW.tar
  raw_dir: data/GSE260661_RAW
  series_soft_url: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE260nnn/GSE260661/soft/GSE260661_family.soft.gz
  series_soft: data/GSE260661_family.soft.gz
  # Curated from Ju et al. 2024, Table 1 (GEO characteristics are wrong for the G2 samples).
  samples: data/samples.tsv
  # Sample id = file name after "GSM<digits>_" without ".txt.gz" (e.g. G1-S1); must match samples.tsv.
  file_pattern: "^GSM[0-9]+_(.+)\\.txt\\.gz$"

samples:
  id_column: sample_id
  patient_column: patient
  timepoint_column: timepoint
  grade_column: ctcae_grade

# Timepoint value in samples.tsv -> label used in the models (valid R names). Positive log2FC = higher in
# `treatment` (the later draw).
groups:
  labels:
    G1: early
    G2: late
  reference: early
  treatment: late
  descriptions:
    early: "first draw, 2–3 FOLFOX cycles"
    late: "second draw, 6–8 FOLFOX cycles"
  colors:
    early: "#3399FF"
    late: "#CC0000"

# Sample ids removed from the analysis.
exclude_samples: []

filter:
  min_count: 10       # reads
  min_samples: 8      # smallest group size (8 patients per timepoint)

# Models fitted with edgeR quasi-likelihood. Variables available: patient, timepoint (factor, early/late),
# delta_grade_c (per-patient CIPN grade change, late - early, centred), late_delta_grade_c (= delta_grade_c on
# the late draw, 0 on the early one: the timepoint × grade-change interaction), plus every samples.tsv column.
# `coef` is the column of the design matrix tested.
models:
  paired:
    formula: "~ patient + timepoint"
    coef: timepointlate
    description: "Within-patient change from the early to the late draw (primary analysis)."
  unpaired:
    formula: "~ timepoint"
    coef: timepointlate
    description: "Late vs early as independent groups, as in the paper (for reference)."
  cipn_worsening:
    formula: "~ patient + timepoint + late_delta_grade_c"
    coef: late_delta_grade_c
    description: "Extra log2FC of the early-to-late change per +1 CIPN grade gained (Δgrade 0, +1, +2)."
primary_model: paired

de:
  # User decision 2026-11-21: no miRNA passes FDR < 0.05 in the primary model, so every model uses the
  # unadjusted p < pvalue_fallback (exploratory). "auto" = FDR, falling back to p only when nothing passes FDR.
  criterion: pvalue
  padj: 0.05             # FDR cutoff (reported; used when criterion is padj/auto)
  pvalue_fallback: 0.01  # unadjusted p-value cutoff
  lfc: 0.5               # minimum |log2FC|

# miRNAs reported by the authors (both higher in the late draw by sequencing; only miR-3184-5p validated
# by qPCR). Shown in every model and in the paired-lines plot.
candidates:
  - hsa-miR-3184-5p
  - hsa-miR-222-3p

# Plasma QC: hemolysis ratio log2(miR-451a / miR-23a-3p) on CPM (qPCR rule: ΔCq > 7 suggests hemolysis).
qc:
  hemolysis_numerator: hsa-miR-451a
  hemolysis_denominator: hsa-miR-23a-3p

plots:
  heatmap_max_mirnas: 40

# Validated targets (multiMiR) of the DE miRNAs of `primary_model`, then GO BP and KEGG over-representation
# with the targets of all tested miRNAs as universe.
targets:
  # Low-throughput, strong evidence only. TarBase (mostly CLIP/high-throughput) was tried on 2026-11-21: 409 k
  # pairs covering 17,493 genes, so every miRNA "targets" most of the genome and the universe is the genome.
  databases: [mirtarbase, mirecords]
  # Only strong evidence (Western blot, luciferase, qPCR) from miRTarBase; set to false to keep every entry.
  mirtarbase_strong_only: true
enrichment:
  orgdb: org.Hs.eg.db
  organism_kegg: hsa
  pvalue_cutoff: 0.05
  min_gs_size: 10
  max_gs_size: 500
  # A target counts only if at least this many DE miRNAs hit it (1 = union of their targets).
  min_mirnas_per_target: 1

seed: 123
